body.statement: Under \(n_{\rm samp}\) independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) with joint multinomial law \(\pi\), the primitive region \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfies \(P_{\pi}(\pi\in\mathcal P_n)\ge1-\alpha\). Consequently, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\subseteq\mathcal C_n(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) simultaneously for every \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\) at which the population target exists.
body.justification: One primitive coverage event protects every budget, orientation tie, and endpoint switch without gridwise multiplicity corrections.
body.gap: Huang et al. give pointwise asymptotic inference for complete outcomes, while Kaido et al. and Cho--Russell give asymptotic projection methods; none gives this finite-sample whole-surface outer guarantee.
body.consumer: The theorem provides an honest default uncertainty display for sensitivity surfaces before design-specific refinements for the Job Corps and Oregon samples.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(M_0=4m(K+1)\), and for observation \(i\) and multinomial category \(j\) let \(I_{ij}\) be its category indicator.  Then \(I_{1j},\ldots,I_{n_{\rm samp}j}\) are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(\pi_j\), and \(\widehat\pi_j=n_{\rm samp}^{-1}\sum_iI_{ij}\).

For completeness, derive the needed Bernoulli tail bound.  If \(a>p\), then for every \(\lambda>0\), exponential Markov inequality and independence give
\[
 \Pr_p(\widehat p\geq a)
 \leq e^{-\lambda n_{\rm samp}a}
      \mathbb E_p\exp\left(\lambda\sum_i I_i\right)
 =\left[e^{-\lambda a}(1-p+pe^\lambda)\right]^{n_{\rm samp}}.
\]
For \(p<a<1\), differentiation gives the minimizing value
\(e^\lambda=a(1-p)/(p(1-a))\), and substitution yields
\[
 \Pr_p(\widehat p\geq a)
 \leq \exp\{-n_{\rm samp}D(a\Vert p)\},
 \qquad
 D(a\Vert p)=a\log\frac ap+(1-a)\log\frac{1-a}{1-p}.
\]
The boundary cases follow by limits.  As a function of \(a\),
\[
 \frac{\partial^2}{\partial a^2}D(a\Vert p)
 =\frac1{a(1-a)}\geq4,
 \qquad D(p\Vert p)=0,
 \qquad \left.\frac{\partial}{\partial a}D(a\Vert p)\right|_{a=p}=0.
\]
Twice integrating the second-derivative inequality yields
\(D(a\Vert p)\geq2(a-p)^2\).  The lower-tail calculation is identical.  Therefore, for every category,
\[
 P_\pi\bigl(|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|>\varepsilon_n\bigr)
 \leq2\exp(-2n_{\rm samp}\varepsilon_n^2)
 =\frac{\alpha}{M_0}.
\]
No independence among the different category counts is used.  The union bound now gives
\[
 P_\pi\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq M_0}
 |\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|\leq\varepsilon_n\right)\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Since \(\pi\) lies in the simplex, the event in parentheses implies \(\pi\in\mathcal P_n\), proving primitive-region coverage.

On this single event, positive covariate masses and assignment overlap imply
\[
 \pi_{xz}=P(X=x,Z=z)>0
\]
for every \(x,z\), so the true arm-conditioning map is defined and the candidate \(\pi' =\pi\) is not omitted from the union defining \(\mathcal C_n\).  It follows deterministically, for every budget pair, that
\[
 \Theta_I(q(\pi);\delta_D,\delta_S)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{\pi'\in\mathcal P_n}
 \Theta_I(q(\pi');\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\mathcal C_n(\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]
The projection--lifting theorem identifies the set on the left with the causal values among compatible full response laws.  Because the same primitive event was used for all budget pairs, the inclusion holds simultaneously on \(\mathcal B\), with no gridwise multiplicity step.  Restricting the statement to points where the population target exists merely excludes empty target sets and does not change the probability bound.
